2: This is <s>vijñaptimātra</s> (consciousness-only), because of the appearance of non-existent objects,
3: just as a person with an eye-disease (<s>taimirika</s>) sees non-existent hairs, moons, and the like. (verse 1)
4: If consciousness is without [real] objects, the regularity of place and time,
5: the irregularity of the [perceiving] mental continuum, and functional efficacy would not be justified. (verse 2)
6: Irregularity of place and the like is established as in a dream; and irregularity of the continuum, as in the case of <s>pretas</s> (hungry ghosts) —
7: when all [of them] see rivers of pus and the like. (verse 3)
8: Functional efficacy [is established] as in the harm caused by dreams; and as in hell —
9: where all see the hell-guardians and the like and are tormented by them. (verse 4)
10: Just as animals are [not] born in heaven, so too not in hell;
11: not for the <s>pretas</s> [are they real beings], because they [the guardians] do not experience the suffering born from that [place]. (verse 5)
12: If the arising of such [hell-guardian] beings there through <s>karma</s> (action) is accepted,
13: why is transformation of consciousness not accepted [instead]? (verse 6)
14: The <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of the <s>karma</s> is in one place, the fruit is imagined in another;
15: why is [the fruit] not accepted right there where the <s>vāsanā</s> is? What is the reason? (verse 7)
16: The existence of the <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases) of form and the like was stated with respect to those beings to be guided,
17: spoken intentionally, like [the reference to] spontaneously born (<s>upapāduka</s>) beings. (verse 8)
18: Since consciousness (<s>vijñapti</s>) arises from its own seed (<s>svabīja</s>), appearing as whatever [object],
19: the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) spoke of those [seeds and appearances] as its twofold <s>āyatanas</s> (sense-bases). (verse 9)
20: Thus [is] the entry into the selflessness of persons (<s>pudgalanairātmya</s>);
21: but the other teaching — the entry into the selflessness of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>dharmanairātmya</s>) — is through the imagined self (<s>kalpitātman</s>) [of dharmas]. (verse 10)
22: That [external object] is neither one nor many; the object, [considered] atom by atom (<s>paramāṇuśas</s>), [does not exist];
23: nor are they combined, because the atom (<s>paramāṇu</s>) is not established. (verse 11)
24: Because of simultaneous conjunction with six [neighbors], the atom would have six parts;
25: if the six share the same location, the aggregate would be merely atom-sized. (verse 12)
26: If the atom has no conjunction, to what [component] does that aggregate belong?
27: And conjunction is not established because of [the atom's] partlessness (<s>anavayavatva</s>). (verse 13)
28: That which has division into directional parts (<s>digbhāgabheda</s>) cannot be one;
29: otherwise, how would there be shadow and obstruction? And if there is no aggregate, these do not belong to it. (verse 14)
30: If [atoms are] one, there would be no gradual movement, no simultaneous apprehension and non-apprehension,
31: no separated manifold activity, and no perception of subtle [atoms]. (verse 15)
32: Perceptual cognition (<s>pratyakṣabuddhi</s>), as in dreams and the like — that [cognition occurs],
33: yet at that time, that object is not seen [to exist]; how then is its perceptual character maintained? (verse 16)
34: As stated, consciousness appears as that [object]; memory arises therefrom.
35: In a dream, one who has not awakened does not understand the absence of the visual object. (verse 17)
36: By mutual dominant causation (<s>anyonyādhipatitva</s>), there is mutual regularity of consciousness.
37: The mind impaired by torpor (<s>middha</s>) in a dream — therefore its fruit is unequal [to waking]. (verse 18)
38: Death [is caused] by the transformation due to the distinctive influence of another's consciousness,
39: just as the loss of memory and the like of others [is caused] by the mental power of <s>piśācas</s> (spirits) and the like. (verse 19)
40: How else [is] the emptying of the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest through the anger of sages [explained]?
41: How else is the great fault of mental punishment (<s>manodaṇḍa</s>) established thereby? (verse 20)
42: How is the knowledge of those who know others' minds not fully accurate? Just as
43: knowledge of one's own mind [is limited] because of ignorance; [perfect knowledge] is the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. (verse 21)
44: This establishment of <s>vijñaptimātratā</s> (consciousness-only), commensurate with my own ability,
45: has been made by me; but that [full reality] in all its aspects is inconceivable — it is the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. (verse 22)
